title: Generic Binary Search Tree
prompt:
Implement a generic binary search tree using Option<Box<Node<T>>> for child links.

Bst<T: Ord> methods:
- new() -> empty tree
- insert(&mut self, value: T) -> bool: insert value; return false (and do nothing) if it was already present.
- contains(&self, value: &T) -> bool
- len(&self) -> usize: number of stored values
- height(&self) -> usize: number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path (empty tree = 0, single node = 1)
- min(&self) -> Option<&T> and max(&self) -> Option<&T>
- in_order(&self) -> Vec<&T>: values in ascending order
- range_count(&self, lo: &T, hi: &T) -> usize: how many stored values v satisfy lo <= v <= hi. Prune subtrees that cannot contain values in range.

Tip: insertion can walk down with a mutable cursor: let mut cur = &mut self.root; while let Some(node) = cur { ... cur = &mut node.left; } — be careful with the borrow checker, a recursive helper is also fine. Note that a degenerate (sorted-input) tree can be thousands of nodes deep; recursion to depth ~3000 is fine with the default test thread stack.

Example:
  insert 5, 3, 8, 1, 4 -> in_order = [1, 3, 4, 5, 8], height = 3, range_count(&2, &5) = 3
